issues.title: Example wanted for equivalenace mapping
issues.author: nacho319
issues.body:
In the paragraph / bullet point of the following:

```
Name strings may be mapped to equivalent names resulting in a
  file having an equivalent name rather than the one specified by
  the client.  This approach is implementable within the server
  proper.
```


I think an example added to that paragraph would be really helpful.

issues.title: Expand UNICODE normalization acronyms
issues.author: nacho319
issues.body:
The draft just starts mentioning ```NFC``` and ```NFD``` without really explaining them; spell out the words before first acronym use and I think some really simple comments about what NFC and NFD are would be helpful.  First use is the following:

```
Generally, when such pairs exist, the form in which the diacritic is
  integrated into the symbol is designated the NFC form while the other is
  the NFD form.
```

and may be some text such as:

```
Unicode Normalization Form C (NFC) is typically described as the canonical decomposition of a character.  Unicode Normalization Form D (NFD) is typically described as the canonical decomposition followed by the canonical composition.  Precomposed characters, single Unicode entries such as (U+00C5) Latin Capital Letter A With Ring Above is precomposed and NFC whereas (U+0041) Latin Capital Letter A + (U+030A) Combining Ring Above are NFD.
```

issues.title: string equivalence and privilege escalation
issues.author: nacho319
issues.body:
In the following snippet, is there a plausible path to privilege escalation:

```
For similar reasons, where non-UTF-8 encoded names are
  accepted, case-related mappings cannot be relied upon.  For
  this reason, the attribute case_insensitive MUST NOT be
  returned as TRUE for file systems which accept non-UTF-8 encoded
  file names.

  The kinds of modification and aliasing mentioned here can lead to both
  false negatives and false positives, depending on the strings in question,
  which can result in security issues such as elevation of privilege and
  denial of service (see {{RFC6943}} for further discussion).
```

Assuming there is strong authentication in place so that we know the identity of the user on the client, shouldn't accessing a sensitive path/file object get denied even if there is some type of crafted string equivalence?
